Every flat map of nonzero domains A→B is injective: for nonzero a in A, flatness preserves the injection A --a→ A after tensoring with B; if a mapped to0, the resulting zero map B→B would be injective, forcing B=0. Hence Frac(A) injects into Frac(B), so transcendence over k cannot disappear. Define G on arrows by identity when both values are Z and by the unique map whenever the target is0. There is no arrow from the transcendental case to the algebraic case; these maps compose exactly, so G is a functor. A filtered diagram of these injections has an integral colimit. Every fraction in the colimit comes from a stage. If every stage fraction field is algebraic over k, every such fraction is algebraic, so G(colim A_i)=Z=colim G(A_i). reason: The source has just weakened X of finite type over k to X noetherian, while requiring the extension field K/k to be finitely generated. The asserted consequence is noetherianity. For an affine open Spec B⊂X, choose a finitely generated integral k-subalgebra A⊂K with Frac(A)=K and put S=A∖{0}. The canonical map b⊗(a/s)↦(b⊗a)/(1⊗s) gives the isomorphism B⊗_k K ≅ S^{-1}(B⊗_k A). The ring B⊗_k A is finitely generated over the noetherian ring B, hence noetherian, and its localization is noetherian. A finite affine cover of X gives a finite such cover of X_K, proving that X_K is noetherian. The printed finite-type-over-the-base conclusion fails in the exact identity-base-change example X=Spec k(u), K=k: X is noetherian and K/k is finitely generated, but X_K=X is not of finite type over k, since Zariski’s lemma would force the field k(u), if finitely generated as a k-algebra, to be finite algebraic over k. This establishes the current replacement and reverses the earlier rejected proposal; it does not insert an additional hypothesis.
